page: Amazon Web Services c8gn.2xlarge is an ARM-based compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by AWS Graviton processors built on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz. The server configuration provides 8 dedicated physical cores with 8 vCPUs at a single thread per core, accompanied by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes 25 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, contains no local storage, and does not feature hardware acceleration GPUs.

Benchmark data demonstrates balanced performance across general compute tasks, alongside standout throughput in memory and decompression workflows. The instance recorded strong results in PassMark memory testing and single-threaded bzip3 decompression, reaching 14.47 GB/sec. General multi-core compute capability is solid, posting a Geekbench multi-core score of 10093.0 and multi-core stress-ng throughput of 13646.63. Memory bandwidth tests yielded 154.1 GB/sec on large block reads and 83.01 GB/sec on large block writes. Performance limitations appear in specialized execution paths: PassMark encryption testing ranked in the lower 25 percent, and medium 7B model prompt processing reached only 15.47 tokens per second.

From an efficiency standpoint, the c8gn.2xlarge delivers predictable compute cycles via non-hyperthreaded physical cores and high network bandwidth per core without the cost overhead of attached local NVMe drives. Because all storage must be provisioned over the network via Elastic Block Store, storage latency and sustained throughput depend entirely on EBS network volume configurations.

The c8gn.2xlarge is suited for network-intensive compute workloads, static web serving, containerized microservices, Clang-based software compilation, and in-memory key-value processing such as Redis. Workloads heavily dependent on large-model machine learning inference or intensive hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives may encounter resource limits on this tier.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gn.2xlarge is an ARMv9 compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and AWS Neoverse-V2 Graviton architecture running at 2.8 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs with 8 physical cores, 16.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core), and a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps. The instance contains no bundled local storage and no GPU accelerators. In synthetic benchmarks, it exhibits top-quartile performance in memory throughput and single-threaded bzip3 decompression, alongside mid-range results across Geekbench multi-core testing, Clang software compilation, and Redis key-value operations. Cryptographic tests and medium-scale LLM prompt evaluation reflect weaker execution tiers. The c8gn.2xlarge delivers predictable CPU throughput without hyperthreading contention, making it appropriate for distributed web serving, software build pipelines, network-intensive microservices, and general compute workloads reliant on external EBS storage.
